headline: Bangladesh Bank introduces KPI framework for bank CEOs to boost accountability
summary: The new system links performance assessments to asset quality, governance, and financial inclusion, directly impacting CEO remuneration and tenure.
details: Bangladesh Bank has launched a uniform Key Performance Indicator (KPI) framework for managing directors and CEOs of scheduled banks. The move aims to strengthen accountability, safeguard depositors' interests, and improve financial stability across the banking sector.
The performance of bank leaders will be assessed across five broad areas: solvency and liquidity, asset quality, governance and internal control, financial inclusion, and profitability.
Weightage is distributed as 25% each for solvency, asset quality, and governance. Inclusion and market conduct account for 15%, while profitability makes up the remaining 10%.
These scores will directly influence CEO remuneration, incentives, benefits, and decisions regarding their appointment, reappointment, and tenure extensions.
A CEO must achieve at least 50% of a predetermined target to receive a score for a specific KPI. If performance falls below this threshold, the score for that indicator will be zero.

The framework introduces penalties for poor performance in six critical areas, including non-performing loan (NPL) ratios and recovery of written-off loans. Scoring zero in these areas will result in a 25% deduction from the overall score.
Bank boards must set targets based on previous quarterly performance and regulatory expectations. For current CEOs, the first assessment period will run from October 1, 2026, to March 31, 2027.
The boards will assess CEOs every six months and submit review reports to the central bank. Bangladesh Bank will review these frameworks and may issue further directives based on the results.

headline_marked: 8 children die in 24 hours as [[measles death toll reaches 1,030]]
headline: 8 children die in 24 hours as measles death toll reaches 1,030
summary: The Directorate General of Health Services reports a surge in suspected measles cases, with over 172,000 nationwide infections recorded this year.
details: Eight children died with measles-like symptoms within a 24-hour period, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
This brings the total number of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths in Bangladesh this year to 1,030.
The DGHS has classified the eight most recent fatalities as suspected measles deaths, contributing to a total of 930 suspected and 100 confirmed deaths.
In the same 24-hour window, 1,177 new suspected cases were reported, raising the nationwide tally to 172,720 suspected infections.
Additionally, 55 new laboratory-confirmed cases were recorded, bringing the total number of confirmed measles infections to 20,124.
Since March 15 this year, 152,117 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalised across the country.
Of those hospitalised, 146,400 patients have recovered.
